overview.title: Training
overview.purpose: Your course: Orientation, Foundations, four competition-module tracks and mock competitions. Pick up where you left off or start with what your test showed.
overview.help: Start with Orientation, then climb the Foundations ladder. The four tracks match the four competition days (M1 to M4). Each level opens when you pass the level before it.
overview.continueNone: You have finished everything that is open to you. Well done.
overview.recommendedText: Based on the skill map from your latest test. The biggest gains come first.
overview.recommendedEmpty: Take the free skills test and we will suggest where to start.
overview.solidworksTitle: You are on the SOLIDWORKS track
overview.solidworksText: The competition uses Autodesk Inventor or Fusion. The SOLIDWORKS track builds the same skills, and we recommend switching to Inventor before competition mocks.
overview.notEnrolledTitle: You are using the free sample
overview.notEnrolledText: Free for you now: all of Orientation, the Foundations Level 1 lessons and the Level 1 exercises with automatic checking. Join the training to open every level, track and mock.
overview.certificatesEmpty: Finish every level of a module to earn its certificate.
overview.instrumentsText: Each instrument you may bring to Module 4, and how to use it.
overview.inPersonText: Measuring practice, 3D scanning, 3D printing and full-length mocks in Lusail.

stats.xpHelp: You earn XP the first time you pass an exercise. Higher levels give more XP. XP is only for you: there is no public leaderboard.
stats.streakHelp: Weeks in a row in which you finished a lesson or uploaded an exercise. One session a week keeps it going.
stats.badgesEmpty: Finish a level to earn your first badge.

ladder.title: Levels
ladder.help: Each level opens when you pass every exercise of the level before it at its pass mark. A level without exercises is done when you finish its lessons. A trainer can also unlock a level for you.

instruments.title: Measuring instruments
instruments.purpose: The instruments you may bring to the reverse engineering module (M4), what each one measures, and a short lesson on using it.
instruments.intro: In Module 4 you measure a real part with hand instruments and sketch it on paper. The part is taken away after 2 hours, so measuring fast and right matters.

digitalCaliper.name: Digital caliper
digitalCaliper.measures: Outside and inside sizes, steps and small depths, read in millimetres.

offsetCaliper.name: Offset centerline caliper
offsetCaliper.measures: Distances between hole centres, and from an edge to a hole centre.

radiusGauges.name: Radius gauges
radiusGauges.measures: Inside and outside radii of rounded edges.

threadGauges.name: Thread pitch gauges
threadGauges.measures: The pitch of external and internal metric threads, so you can name the thread.
threadGauges.range: 0.35-6 mm pitch; M6, M8, M10 and M12 plugs

roughness.name: Surface roughness (Ra) comparator
roughness.measures: How rough a machined surface is, by comparing it with reference samples.

depthGauge.name: Depth gauge caliper
depthGauge.measures: The depth of holes, pockets and steps.

instruments.also: A 3D mouse, your own keyboard and mouse, and a standards book or manuals.
instruments.kitTitle: Get a student measuring kit from Gestaltung360

inPerson.title: In-person sessions
inPerson.purpose: What happens at our studio in Lusail: measuring practice, 3D scanning, 3D printing and full-length mock competitions.

what.measuring: Measuring practice on real parts with the allowed instruments.
what.scanning: 3D scanning basics: what a scan can and cannot tell you.
what.printing: 3D printing your own parts and checking how they fit.
what.mocks: Full-length mock competitions under the real rules.

inPerson.m4Text: Our M4 practice follows the competition rules:

m4.collect: You have the physical part for 2 hours. Then it is collected and you continue from your own sketches.
m4.noCopy: No photos, putty, ink pads or any other way of copying the shape.
m4.computer: Your computer stays available the whole time.

inPerson.m4Help: Module 4 (M4) is the reverse engineering part of the competition: you measure a real part and rebuild it in CAD.

bring.laptop: A laptop with your CAD software installed
bring.notebook: A notebook and pencil for sketches
